newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Japan should reassure China on U.S. ties - Lee.
newsitem.headline: Japan should reassure China on U.S. ties - Lee.

text.p: Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew said on Tuesday Japan should allay Chinese fears that its broadened security alliance with the United States was aimed at containing China or keeping it separate from Taiwan.
"Japan can resolve or reduce these suspicions and allow economic forces to pull Japan and China closer together," Lee, told a symposium in Osaka. A copy of his speech was released in Singapore.

Lee, Singapore's prime minister from 1959 to 1990, said the United States remained key to integrating China into the international community but there would always be some tension between the two because China had the potential to challenge U.S. economic dominance in time.

"The Chinese people will change in order to plug into the global community to maximise their growth and development," he said, adding however, that the pace of change would be in keeping with China's history and culture.

Lee said the United States, Europe, Japan and Southeast Asian countries should give China an incentive to observe international rules and conventions by rewarding it when it did so with increased trade, investment and economic cooperation.
"As China's economy becomes more externally orientated, it will become interdependent with the major trading countries of the world," he said.
